newsitem.title: USA: Progress seen in Los Angeles sports arena talks.
newsitem.headline: Progress seen in Los Angeles sports arena talks.

text.p: City of Los Angeles negotiators have made "substantial progress" in talks for a proposed downtown sports complex, prompting officials to set a city council hearing for December 3 to consider the deal.

"Over the past weeks, substantial progress has been made toward reaching agreement on the deal points," Los Angeles Council President John Ferraro and Councilmember Rita Walters said in a joint statement on Tuesday.
"Our city negotiators have advised that while 95 percent of the issues have been resolved, a handful of deal points remain outstanding," the statement said.
In order to expedite the decision-making process, the statement said the full city council would consider the arena proposal and the remaining deal points at a meeting on December 3.
"Time is of the essence," the statement said.

As proposed last summer, city taxpayers would provide the land and developers would build and operate the $200 million sports complex, which would house the Kings hockey team and the Lakers basketball team.
Under the plan, the city would issue about $60.5 million of bonds to acquire and clear land for the arena at the Los Angeles Convention Center.
